builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Syllable- and Word-Level Evaluation of Tibetan OCR
summary: It replaces sole reliance on character error rate with syllable error rate and segmented word error rate for Tibetan OCR evaluation. It adds evaluation complexity and requires a segmenter only for SWER, while SER avoids that dependency and needs no model or infrastructure change. CER can fail because it may reverse the ranking of a system pair and does not establish which systems preserve named entities at 0.6.
rationale: The reader can adopt SER immediately as a low-cost, segmenter-free metric that correlates strongly with word-level ranking and better reflects downstream utility than CER alone.
technique: Syllable and word error rates for Tibetan OCR

claims.statement: It replaces sole reliance on character error rate with syllable error rate and segmented word error rate for Tibetan OCR evaluation. It adds evaluation complexity and requires a segmenter only for SWER, while SER avoids that dependency and needs no model or infrastructure change. CER can fail because it may reverse the ranking of a system pair and does not establish which systems preserve named entities at 0.6.
CER ranks systems largely as the higher-level rates do (Kendall tau >= 0.833), with one pair ordered oppositely; SER ranks systems as SWER does under two of three segmenters (tau >= 0.889).
